chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

"Prayer during travel is two rak'ahs; there is nothing before them or after them except for Maghrib, for after it are four rak'ahs; do not leave them in residence or in travel. And there is no making up (qada) for you of the daytime prayer, and pray the night prayer and make it up."
ai.seo_question: What are the rules for shortening prayers and handling missed prayers during travel in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the specific structure of the four-unit travel prayer (Salat al-Musafir), emphasizing the unique status of Maghrib which retains its four rak'ahs even during travel, unlike Dhuhr, Asr, and Isha. It further clarifies the ruling on Qada (making up missed prayers), indicating that while missed daytime prayers do not require compensation in this context, the night prayer (Isha) must be performed and made up, reflecting the distinct spiritual weight assigned to night worship in Shia jurisprudence. This hadith is foundational in the chapter of supererogatory prayers during travel, highlighting the balance between ease (rukhas) and continuity of worship.
